claims.statement: The EUDR Information System accepts bulk GeoJSON origins and lets downstream parties refer to upstream statements using reference and verification numbers.
Official guidance says required information includes geolocation of all production plots and adequately conclusive, verifiable evidence of deforestation-free and lawful production.

contrary_evidence: The official Information System already offers manual, CSV and GeoJSON workflows, and the latest amendments delay application for many operators; low-risk sourcing can simplify diligence.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: cross-buyer library of resolved polygon, land-right and upstream-reference defects without exposing buyer-confidential data
fingerprint.customer: EU commodity importers and downstream operators buying from fragmented farms and forestry suppliers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: commodity ERP, trade-finance and certification-workflow partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: multi-buyer supplier evidence identity, GeoJSON QA and reference-chain vault sold per plot and lot
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: importer pays when a supplier plot is maintained and a shipment lot obtains a complete evidence bundle
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a relevant commodity lot lacks reusable plot-level traceability before market placement or export

founder_fit: Excellent geospatial/data-quality and AI-document fit with asynchronous channel distribution. UNVALIDATED HYPOTHESIS: PLN 90000 is enough for a narrow one-commodity pilot; no field inspection is promised.
risks: Bad plot evidence can halt trade and create liability.
Remote sensing cannot itself prove land rights or lawful production.

structure.control_point: commodity purchase-lot release after plot and reference-number resolution
structure.critical_dependency: supplier-provided plot geolocation and lawful-production documents with reuse permission

thesis: Create a shared geospatial evidence utility for coffee, cocoa, wood and rubber supply chains that normalises plot polygons, lawful-origin evidence and upstream due-diligence references before a purchase lot is released. Reuse across buyers gives suppliers one maintained evidence identity while a resolution corpus learns which plot and chain-of-custody defects block a statement.
title: EUDR Plot-Evidence Utility
uncertainties: Supplier consent to reuse evidence across buyers
How much national enforcement practice differs
